question: What is the primary mode of transmission for sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Inhalation of airborne droplets from coughing
options.B: Unprotected sexual contact with an infected partner
options.C: Direct contact with contaminated swimming pool water
options.D: Sharing eating utensils in public canteens

explanation: Pathogens responsible for STIs are primarily spread through genital, oral, or anal contact involving infected bodily fluids or mucous membranes. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h1)

question: How do viral STIs differ from bacterial STIs in the body?

options.A: Viral agents only attack outer skin layers
options.B: Bacterial pathogens are immune to all medicines
options.C: Viral infections often stay in host cells for life
options.D: Bacterial infections never cause any symptoms

explanation: Viruses like HIV and HSV persist within host cells for life, whereas bacterial infections are typically cured with appropriate antibiotics. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention in community health?

options.A: Stopping new infections before they happen in healthy people
options.B: Tracing past sexual partners of a patient
options.C: Treating severe inflammation in hospital wards
options.D: Curing chronic viral diseases after symptoms appear

explanation: Primary prevention focuses on risk reduction and protective measures to keep healthy individuals from contracting an infection in the first place. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which infection is directly prevented by the routine HPV vaccine?
explanation: The human papillomavirus vaccine targets strains responsible for cervical changes, genital warts, and related cancers. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h3)

question: How do vaccines protect people against viral STIs?

options.A: By changing vaginal pH to kill foreign cells
options.B: By destroying bacterial cell walls in the blood
options.C: By replacing damaged tissues in the reproductive tract
options.D: By helping the body make antibodies before natural exposure

explanation: Vaccines introduce harmless antigens that prompt the immune system to build long-term defense memories against the actual virus. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h3)

question: Why is routine screening important for controlling sexually transmitted infections?

options.A: Many infected people do not show visible symptoms
options.B: Lab tests can permanently immunize patients against reinfection
options.C: Swabs remove the need for any antibiotics
options.D: Screening replaces the need for condoms

explanation: Asymptomatic carriers can unknowingly transmit infections, so routine screening detects hidden cases early. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h4)

question: Which test is considered the best standard for detecting Chlamydia and Gonorrhea?
explanation: NAAT provides high sensitivity and specificity by detecting genetic material found in urine or swab samples. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why must patients finish all prescribed antibiotics for a bacterial STI?

options.B: To ensure all bacteria are gone and prevent drug resistance
options.D: To avoid needing follow-up blood tests

explanation: Stopping antibiotics early can leave surviving bacteria behind, leading to treatment failure and resistant strains. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h5)

question: What is usually done in clinics when lab test results are delayed?

options.C: Waiting for final culture reports before doing anything

explanation: Syndromic management treats recognized groups of symptoms immediately to reduce complications and stop ongoing transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h5)

question: Why is partner notification important when treating a patient with an STI?

options.A: It permanently clears the virus from the index patient
options.B: It stops the cycle of reinfection between partners
options.C: It removes the need for barrier methods
options.D: It provides financial help for clinic visits

explanation: Treating partners simultaneously prevents reinfecting the original patient and halts community spread. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is Expedited Partner Therapy in STI care?

options.A: Using security officers to track down contacts
options.B: Mailing lab test kits to homes
options.C: Giving prescriptions or medicine to partners without a clinic visit
options.D: Mandatory hospital admission for exposed people

explanation: EPT allows quick treatment delivery to exposed partners, overcoming barriers that prevent them from visiting a clinic. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h6)

question: How does social stigma negatively impact STI control in healthcare?

options.A: It discourages people from seeking early testing and treatment
options.B: It stops nurses from giving vaccines

explanation: Fear of judgment or shame drives patients away from clinics, delaying vital diagnoses and increasing transmission. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h7)

question: Which quality is most important for a nurse taking a sexual history from a client?

options.A: Rushing through the interview to save time
options.B: Involving family members in the talk

explanation: Creating a safe, private, and accepting environment builds trust and encourages accurate health disclosures. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h7)
